text:
jordan: Quick Q — saw a bunch of pods get evicted during a Karpenter scale-in while the HPA was doing bursty downscaling. Pods log showed SIGTERM, but some failed readiness reattach and restarted. Anyone seen this pattern?

sam: Yup. Usually an interplay between aggressive provisioner consolidation, short TTLs, and pods that have long terminationGracePeriod or slow shutdown. Do we have PDBs set?

maya: We do, but it's pretty permissive: `minAvailable: 1` for many stateful-ish pods. Also some pods don't implement a preStop hook so they are killed mid-work.

raj: One thing to check: our terraform change last week lowered `ttlSecondsUntilExpired` on the karpenter provisioner to 60s to make nodes recycle faster. That reduces how long nodes hang around after scale-in signal which can exacerbate mid-shutdown evictions.

emily: Oof. For reference, here's the HPA snippet we run for the service that saw the most failures:
```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: inference-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: inference
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 20
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 55
```

sam: Two actionable levers: 1) tighten PDBs for critical pods + set podPriority so low-priority pods get evicted first, 2) increase provisioner TTL and/or disable consolidation during heavy bursts.

maya: Also add a small preStop that lets in-flight work finish and make readiness probe more conservative so the pod gets traffic drained before SIGTERM: e.g. `preStop: exec: ["/bin/sleep", "10"]` and `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30`.

raj: For the Terraform side, current change looks like:
```hcl
resource "karpenter_provisioner" "default" {
  spec {
    consolidation { enabled = true }
    ttlSecondsUntilExpired = 60
    limits { resources { cpu = "1000" } }
  }
}
```
If we change ttlSecondsUntilExpired => 300 it gives pods more time to drain. Also consider `consolidation.enabled = false` for short windows using a feature flag.

emily: For testing, we should simulate burst scale-downs: run load to bump replicas to 15, then drop traffic and watch Karpenter/CA behavior. Use `kubectl cordon/drain` to emulate and check PDB blocking. Also confirm `--eviction-hard` kubelet thresholds aren't being hit (disk pressure can cause forced evictions).

jordan: Good checklist. One more: does the cluster-autoscaler exist alongside Karpenter in this cluster? We had a hybrid flag in staging before. If both are active they can conflict on scale decisions.

sam: We removed CA from prod months ago, but staging still has `cluster-autoscaler` deployed for some legacy nodegroups. Confirmed: that may race with karpenter's consolidation.

opsbot: Incident note created: INC-2026-013 - investigation into HPA-triggered evictions during Karpenter scale-in. Link: https://redwood-internal/incident/INC-2026-013

maya: Proposed quick mitigations:
- Increase `ttlSecondsUntilExpired` to 300 in prod provisioner via terraform PR.
- Add `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30` + simple preStop to pods that are failing.
- Tighten PDBs for core services and add priorityClass for best-effort workers.
- Run chaos test in staging to simulate burst downscaling.

emily: I'll draft the terraform + k8s manifest PRs and a test plan for staging. Want to include a smoke test that asserts no restarts within 90s after scale-in.

jordan: Thanks all — please @sam or @maya if you want to pair on the PR reviews. I'll link the PR to INC-2026-013.

sam: FYI, if we need faster ops rollback we can toggle `consolidation.enabled` remotely (if we expose it in SSM/console) before the full terraform apply. Good to have as emergency button.

jordan: Cool. I'll start the terraform PR and a short runbook for oncall.

emily: PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482 (WIP)

jordan: Awesome — assigning follow-ups in the PR. :thumbsup:
